speaker: Patient
text: Newborn, born at 33 weeks of gestation. The newborn is presenting with respiratory distress 2 hours after birth. The mother had an uneventful pregnancy until premature onset of labor. There was no significant prenatal care history mentioned.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the details; your preterm birth at 33 weeks and immediate respiratory distress are significant. I see the chest X-ray is coming, but while waiting for the image, have you noticed any "grunting" breaths or flaring of your nostrils?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Respiratory distress. I also have Grunting, Intercoastal and subcostal retractions, Peripheral cyanosis.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Thank you for confirming the presence of grunting and retractions; these physical findings, combined with your respiratory acidosis and hypoxemia, are classic signs of significant respiratory distress. Given your history of prematurity at 33 weeks, I strongly suspect Respiratory Distress Syndrome; please review the attached chest X-ray image carefully.

DIAGNOSIS READY: Respiratory Distress Syndrome (RDS)
